paragraphs.text: Third-party cloud and identity providers have become primary attack vectors, with a Railway infrastructure breach exposing authentication secrets for up to 100,000 workspaces and compromised Qubole IAM credentials enabling cross-customer AWS data exfiltration. Simultaneously, a major retailer lost 37.6 million customer records through unauthorized system access. These events demonstrate that supplier identity boundaries and data protection controls are being bypassed at scale, requiring immediate review of third-party access scope, credential management and supplier assurance evidence.

Vulnerability management faces unprecedented volume and supply-chain reach, with Microsoft releasing patches for nearly 1,100 vulnerabilities including 63 critical flaws and an actively exploited Outlook zero-day, while a Git integer truncation flaw allows malicious code execution during routine recursive clone operations across development pipelines. An AhsayCBS authentication bypass chain has also been actively exploited. Control owners must verify asset coverage, patch deployment and compensating controls across both production systems and development toolchains.
